title: Double bass
summary: Four open strings (E1, A1, D2, G2) and three stopped notes. D3 is bowed at 0.1286 of its sounding length and locks to one fast slip per period at all three bow cells (read with the flyback reader, which does not count slow secondary slips; the page before it, without the bridge's residual-flexibility row, also read one at every cell, with a slow secondary slip at the third); it carries that row, and sounds 2.6 cents flat of equal temperament on the 23-layer rib (8.0 sharp without the row, 7.1 on the 6-layer rib). Eb2, stopped on the A string with 512 body modes, the bass's own bow-hair row and the bridge's residual-flexibility row, sounds 0.4 cents sharp of equal temperament (7.1 without the row) and slips fast once per period at all three bow cells (flyback reader). Db4, stopped on the D string with 512 body modes, the bass's own bow-hair row, the bridge's residual-flexibility row and the bow at one eleventh of the sounding length, sounds its note 0.9 cents flat of equal temperament on the 23-layer rib (14.4 sharp without the row), and by the flyback reader its bow slips fast once per period at all three cells, with the row and without it; the raw count of the page before the row at its centre cell (no slip in 64 of 265 periods, once in 114 and twice in 87, where the page with the violin row slipped once in 263 of 264) had read it as unlocked, and the other reader's count there rises with the row from 1.08 to 1.83 entries per period while the fast count stays at 1.00. A1 and G2 at 512 modes carry the bass's own row too (D2 does not: it plays the render of 2026-11-04 with the violin row). A1 carries four strings on the bridge (the bowed A string and the unbowed E, D and G) and slips fast twice per period at all three bow cells on the plate-C page and once on the four-string page before it, with the 0.0162 surrogate (the flyback reader; the one-string page on the 23-layer rib before that slipped twice, and the 6-layer page once, as the 256-mode page did), and by the same reader D2 slips fast twice per period at all three cells on the 23-layer rib and G2 once; the raw counts of their centre cells, four to six and two to four times per period, include slow secondary slips. The body is a computed shell that keeps its lowest 512 modes on every page but D2, which keeps 256 and ends at 1623.53 Hz (the top of the first window of 256 modes): to 2875.75 Hz on the 6-layer rib of the E1 and G2 pages, and to 2417.44 Hz on the 23-layer rib of the A1, D3, Eb2 and Db4 pages (2535.41 Hz at 12 layers; the 512th mode is the top of the second window of 256 modes, computed on 2026-11-06). Above the last mode it neither moves nor radiates, so the pages are much darker than the recordings from about 3 kHz up. The rib is not converged at 6 layers: going to 23 layers moves the median of the first 100 coupled modes down 76 cents (4.3 %) and of ranks 201 to 257 down 164 cents (9.0 %), and the 23-layer rib is within about 0.24 % of its limit on the first 100 modes and about 1 % at 1.2 to 1.45 kHz by extrapolation; above 1.45 kHz it is not shown. It is spruce and maple shell with a 116 L air cavity through the f-holes, from Johannsson's printed bass dimensions on the cello shell route, not a scan; wood below 150 Hz is a declared extrapolation. The maple's radial loss factor is the measured 0.0240 of violin-back plate C (Alkadri et al. 2018) on the G2, Eb2, D3, Db4 and A1 pages and the surrogate 0.0162 (the longitudinal-shear value) on the E1 and D2 pages; in the lowest ten shell modes in vacuo the measured value lowers the modal quality factor by 2.3 to 15.9 % (median 9.2 %) and moves no mode frequency. On the E1, D2, G2, Eb2, D3, Db4 and A1 pages the levels of H1 to H8 move by at most 0.31 dB (E1), 0.73 dB (D2), 1.05 dB (G2), 8.21 dB (Eb2), 2.20 dB (D3), 1.09 dB (Db4) and 19.08 dB (A1) with every other input of the page it replaces unchanged (the live D2 and G2 were rendered on ts2 and their plate-C pages on ts1), and the grades are E1 3 of 14, D2 8 of 14, Db4 7 of 14 and A1 13 of 14 as before, G2 10 of 14 against 11 (STFT distance left the ruler), D3 8 of 14 against 9 (spectral flux left the ruler; strict 7 against 8) and Eb2 12 of 14 as before (strict 12 against 9); on Eb2 the bow slips fast 1.60, 1.82 and 1.60 times per period at the three cells where the page it replaces slips 2.22, 2.26 and 2.21, and on A1 2.01 times per period at all three cells where the page it replaces slips 1.00, a change of regime on both. The bow is a 10 mm ribbon (16 mm, the bass's own row, on A1, Eb2, Db4 and G2; D3, E1 and D2 keep the violin row) with hair compliance on the measured rosin curve (Woodhouse and Galluzzo 2025, eq. 13). The after-length is 0.184 of the speaking length on the G2, D3, Eb2, Db4 and A1 pages, read from one museum photograph (Metropolitan Museum 504228, +-7 %: 0.171 to 0.197); the E1 page has one sixth of the speaking length (a printed rule) and the D2 page one sixth times 116/115, the cello's printed ratio, borrowed. On the D3, E1, G2, Eb2, D2, Db4 and A1 pages the levels of H1 to H8 move by at most 3.03 dB (D3), 11.80 dB (E1), 3.45 dB (G2), 3.48 dB (Eb2), 4.12 dB (D2), 4.43 dB (Db4) and 17.92 dB (A1), with the card's after-length rows and the stations rescaled with them (and, on D3, Eb2 and Db4, the stop's station) the only inputs changed from the page it replaces, and the grades are D3 8 of 14 as before (strict 7 as before), E1 3 of 14 as before (strict 2 as before), G2 10 of 14 as before (strict 10 as before), Eb2 11 of 14 against 12 (strict 11 against 12), D2 11 of 14 against 10 (strict 10 against 9), Db4 7 of 14 as before (strict 7 as before) and A1 13 of 14 as before (strict 13 as before). On the stopped D3 and Db4 the bow's exact static residual flexibility is carried as well (a card row; the engine admits it beside fixed finger stops since wire a9c5f2e77), rendered on OliveDove's tbc build against a control on the same build without the row, and the levels of H1 to H8 move by at most 0.89 dB (D3) and 1.98 dB (Db4) against that control's, and the grades are D3 9 of 14 against 8 (strict 8 against 7) and Db4 7 of 14 as before (strict 7 as before). On 2026-11-10 the owner's ruling that a page changes only at or above the note's best count put the earlier renders of E1 (rendered 2026-11-06), G2 (rendered 2026-11-05) and D2 (rendered 2026-11-04) back on the site, each scoring higher on the site's grader than the page it replaced. The E1 and D2 pages play the 6-layer rib (512 modes on E1, 256 on D2), the surrogate maple loss 0.0162, no string loss and the earlier after-length, with the violin bow row (7.28 N and 2.72 N); the G2 page was then replaced by a render on the 6-layer rib that carries plate C, the 0.184 after-length and the surrogate string loss (12 of 14 as the render it replaced, at a total distance of 8.49 against 8.57), with the bass row at 1.91 N. The figures above that name the E1, D2 or G2 page with plate C, the surrogate string loss, the 0.184 after-length, the bass row or the 23-layer rib describe, for E1 and D2, renders that are now in those pages' histories, not the sound playing; for G2 they describe the 23-layer renders, which are in its history.
physics_present: computed double-bass shell body: spruce top and bass bar, maple back, ribs and bridge, from Johannsson's printed bass dimensions on the cello shell route; every page but D2 keeps the lowest 512 modes, ending at 2875.75 Hz on the 6-layer rib (E1, G2) and at 2417.44 Hz on the 23-layer rib (A1, D3, Eb2, Db4), and D2 keeps 256, ending at 1623.53 Hz on the 6-layer rib; the rib is meshed with 6 layers through its height on the first group and 23 on the second; first structural mode 106 Hz
air cavity of 116 L breathing through the f-holes (a physical neck); coupled air mode 61 Hz

wood from the measured spruce (from 100 Hz) and maple (from 150 Hz) packs, with the lower band edge moved to 90 Hz as a declared extrapolation, not a measurement; the maple's radial loss factor is the measured 0.0240 of violin-back plate C (Alkadri et al. 2018, Table 1) on the G2, Eb2, D3, Db4 and A1 pages and the surrogate 0.0162 on the E1 and D2 pages, and the maple's two other shear loss factors stay surrogates

Thomastik Spirocore Orchestra 4/4 medium strings (maker's tension table, line mass and gauges) at a 1.100 m speaking length, bending modes in two polarisations, with a bending stiffness; on A1 the E, D and G strings share the bridge with the bowed A string, unbowed and in one polarisation, with the same surrogate loss as the A string, at bridge nodes 27.1, 31.7 and 26.8 mm apart (85.5 mm from E to G, where Johannsson prints one spacing of 85 mm for four strings); on the G2, D3, Eb2, Db4 and A1 pages the string also carries two constant loss factors of 1/900, a declared surrogate (see what is missing); the E1 and D2 pages carry no string loss

bow of finite width: a 10 mm ribbon of 3 cells with hair compliance (Pitteroff and Woodhouse 1998); on A1, Eb2, Db4 and G2 the bass's own row, a 16 mm ribbon with 127 hairs in contact over 0.53 m, which gives the S 1.9e5 N/m and D 31 kg/s they print for a bass bow; D3, E1 and D2 carry the violin row (S 6.1e4 N/m, D 10 kg/s)
friction law measured on real rosin (Woodhouse and Galluzzo 2025, eq. 13), a steady sliding curve

static compliance of the string's omitted bending modes, the ones past the 64 retained, at the bridge and under the bow (exact static Green) on the open pages and on the stopped D3 and Db4 (the engine admits the bow's beside fixed finger stops since wire a9c5f2e77; those two pages were rendered on OliveDove's tbc build, which contains it, and a control without the row on that build reproduces the posted page byte for byte); the stopped Eb2 carries the bridge's alone, since its render with the bow's row graded 11 of 14 against the page's 12 (see what is missing)

after-length (bridge to tailpiece): 0.184 of the speaking length on the G2, D3, Eb2, Db4 and A1 pages, read from one photograph of a bass (Metropolitan Museum 504228, +-7 %: 0.171 to 0.197); one sixth of the speaking length (a printed rule) on the E1 page and that times 116/115, the cello's printed ratio, borrowed, on the D2 page
a bow gesture on a fixed schedule: a 0.15 s ramp to the note's force at 0.15 m/s, then a 20 ms lift; each page states its bow force

a finger stop on the stopped notes (D3, Eb2, Db4): a normal contact on the string at the equal-tempered station; its limit (1000 N on D3, Eb2 and Db4) is the solver's guard, not a finger's force, and no print gives a finger force
physics_missing: body modes above the 512th: above the last one (1623.53 Hz at 256 modes, which is the live D2 page; 2875.75 Hz on the 6-layer rib, 2535.41 Hz at 12 layers, 2417.44 Hz on the 23-layer rib) the body neither moves nor radiates, and the pages are much darker than the recordings from about 3 kHz up. D2 reads 10 of 14 at 512 modes with the bass row against 12 at 256, mostly because the grader reads a shorter sustain on that clip

the rib's convergence: rank by rank in frequency, going from 6 layers to 12 moves the median of the first 100 coupled modes down 58 cents (3.3 %), ranks 101 to 200 by 104 cents (5.8 %) and ranks 201 to 257 by 123 cents (6.9 %); going from 12 layers to 23 moves them a further 13 cents (0.73 %), 28 cents (1.6 %) and 37 cents (2.1 %); a power law in the layer count puts the 23-layer modes about 0.24 % above their limit on the first 100 and about 1.1 % over ranks 201 to 257 (1.2 to 1.45 kHz), an extrapolation; the second window of the 23-layer rib ends at 2417.44 Hz (computed on 2026-11-06; its shifts against the 6- and 12-layer modes are not shown on this card), and the step from 6 layers to 12 moves the 256 modes above the first window by 164 cents (9.0 %) and 203 cents (11.1 %), so the upper part of the 512 modes is not shown to be converged; on G2 the same card (plate C, the 0.184 after-length, the surrogate string loss, bow 1.91 N, 512 modes) rendered for 3 s with the rib at 6, 12 and 23 layers grades 12, 11 and 10 of 14 (strict 12, 11 and 10) at total distances to the recording of 8.49, 9.64 and 9.90, with the odd/even level of the harmonics at -11.94, -6.18 and -3.19 dB against the recording's -13.62 dB and the retained modes ending at 2875.75, 2535.41 and 2417.44 Hz, so the finer rib costs G2 grade and distance monotonically over this ladder; the same card on the 6-layer rib with only 418 retained modes (the modes then end at about 2417 Hz, the band edge of the 23-layer rib at 512 modes; an estimate from the mean mode density, not a computed edge) grades 11 of 14 (strict 11) at a total distance of 9.25 with the odd/even level at -11.92 dB, so the retained band edge accounts for about four fifths of the growth of the STFT, wavelet and cepstral-envelope gaps from 6 to 23 layers (4.34 of 5.29, 2.85 of 3.68 and 3.74 of 4.75 dB), about half of the growth of the total distance (0.76 of 1.41) and one of the two lost counts (the wavelet gap leaves the ruler), and none of the fall of the odd/even level (0.02 of 8.74 dB), which follows the rib mesh. Against the 6-layer pages graded on the same footing (the live page's raw render), the 23-layer rib reads D3 8 of 14 as before (strict 8 against 8), E1 on the bass hair at 11 N 3 against 6 (strict 2 against 5), D2 8 against 10 (strict 8 against 9), G2 11 against 12 (strict 11 against 12), Db4 7 against 6 (strict 6 against 6) and A1 13 against 13 (strict 13 against 13); the A1 page on the 23-layer rib slips fast twice per period at all three cells where the page it replaces slips once, and its gaps grow on the centroid (1.1 to 6.1 semitones), odd/even balance (1.4 to 5.8 dB), harmonics-to-noise (1.1 to 3.2 dB), spectral distance (13.8 to 14.9), STFT distance (14.7 to 15.6), harmonic level pattern (11.9 to 12.6), third-octave envelope (7.0 to 7.8) and fundamental frequency (1.3 to 1.8 cents); seven of its harmonics are lower than on the page it replaces (H4 by 12 dB, H7 21, H8 22, H9 13, H10 11, H11 7, H12 12), and its bow slipped fast once per period at every cell where that page slipped twice (the plate-C A1 page slips twice again); with the bridge's residual flexibility the D3 page on the 23-layer rib reads 9 of 14 against 8 (strict 8 against 8), its gaps growing on the cepstral envelope (20.5 to 21.7), wavelet distance (20.3 to 21.3), STFT distance (24.6 to 25.4), partial frequencies (0.63 to 1.3 cents), odd/even balance (5.0 to 5.6 dB, which leaves the strict ruler as the harmonic level pattern enters it), partial trajectories (8.3 to 8.5), spectral flux (0.78 to 0.92) and the third-octave envelope (8.1 to 8.2); that render is on the gate build and the page before it on the cap-only build, and no render separates the row from the build

stopped notes: D3 sits 14 cents sharp of its recording, and its bow locks only at the centre, the third port slipping twice in most periods; Eb2 with the bridge's residual-flexibility row sounds 0.4 cents sharp of equal temperament where the recording is 6.4 cents sharp, so it sits 5.8 cents flat of it (the page before the row sat within 0.5 cents), its fourth harmonic is 15 dB under the recording's and its second and third 7 and 10 dB over, and it reads 10 of 14 against 12 (strict 7 against 10), STFT distance and attack time leaving the loose ruler and those two with the third-octave envelope the strict one; that render is on the stop-check build and the page before it on the first build, and no render separates the row from the build; the page before the row finished only after four changes at once (512 modes, the bass hair row, the 1000 N guard and a raised-limit binary) and could not say which let it finish; Db4 with the bridge's residual-flexibility row sounds 0.9 cents flat of equal temperament where the recording is 10.9 cents flat, so it sits 10.0 cents sharp of the recording (the grader's gap goes from 25.4 to 10.0 cents), its harmonics are 11 to 45 dB under the recording's from H2 to H12 (H2 by 11 dB, H3 24, H4 27, H5 11, H6 16, H7 20, H8 16, H9 45, H10 42, H11 41, H12 42), so the centroid is 309 Hz against 789 Hz (383 Hz on the page before the row) and the attack reads 214 ms against the recording's 5 ms (67 ms before the row); it reads 7 of 14 as the page before it does (strict 7 against 6), centroid leaving the loose ruler as fundamental frequency enters it, and its gaps grow on the STFT distance (39.5 to 42.0), wavelet distance (24.2 to 26.6), cepstral envelope (23.9 to 26.0) and spectral distance (28.2 to 29.9); that render is on the stop-check build and the page before it on the render-cap build, and no render separates the row from the build

the bass bow-hair row (Pitteroff and Woodhouse 1998, S 1.9e5 N/m, D 31 kg/s) did not raise the grade on A1, Db4, D2 or G2, against the same card with the violin row graded the same way: A1 13 of 14 against 13 (strict 13 against 13), its bow slipping fast once per period at all three cells on the 6-layer rib, as the 256-mode page did (flyback reader); Db4 6 of 14 against 6 (strict 6 against 5) with its lock gone, its attack at 94 ms against 11 ms and its fundamental 24.9 cents from the recording's against 21.8; D2 10 against 10 (strict 9 against 10: the third-octave envelope moves in, the wavelet spectrum out); G2 12 against 12 (strict 12 against 12). Eb2, the page before the residual-flexibility row, reads 12 against 10, with four changes at once as stated above. On the 23-layer rib the flyback reader reads D2 at two fast slips per period at all three cells at the force it had with the violin hair, and G2, Db4 and Eb2 at one (the raw counts of D2, G2 and Db4 had read them as unlocked); E1 at 11 N holds one slip per period in 39 of 39 periods by the stamped rule, which does not count one-row slips, where the flyback reader counts them and reads its centre cell at 3.0 fast slips per period (1.2 without them)

pages with the bass row that did not post: D3 at 512 modes graded 6 of 14 against 8 and lost the lock it had (three to five slips in a period, in 140 periods), and on the 23-layer rib at 3.86 N it grades 7 of 14 (strict 6) against 8 (8), losing harmonics-to-noise (19.7 dB against the recording's 29.2) and, strictly, the odd/even balance, with one fast slip per period at all three cells (flyback reader), so D3 stays on the violin row; E1 with the bass row at the violin-hair force of 7.28 N graded 5 of 14 against 6 and lost its lock (one slip in only 7 of 39 periods), so the E1 page keeps the violin row at 7.28 N; a later E1 render with the bass row at 11 N, the lowest of 11, 14 and 17 N at which a short render of the bass-hair card held the lock (39 of 39 periods; 14 N and 17 N did not), graded 3 of 14 (strict 2) on the 23-layer rib against 6 (5), with 39 of 39 periods locked, and was replaced by the earlier render on 2026-11-10; the bass-hair forces of D2, G2 and Db4 are the violin-hair ones and were not re-laddered

the melody (Ode to Joy, first phrase) on the bass's own bow-hair row is rendered on the 6-layer rib, not on the 23-layer rib of the A1, D3, Eb2 and Db4 pages, whose modes lie lower (the E1, D2 and G2 pages are on the 6-layer rib); the 23-layer melody is not rendered. Its five distinct renders (G2, A2, B2, C3 and D3, cut into 15 slots) are on one build, the stop-check build, because C3 runs only there: the first build refused it 0.358 s in (modal contact residual 2.61e-10 N exceeds 2.16e-10 N after 821 iterations). G2, A2 and D3 are byte for byte the first build's clips; B2 differs from its first-build clip from 0.701 s on (first differing sample 33653, one least-significant bit, then the stick/slip history forks), as the B1 card does from 0.218 s, with the regime the same in both. The cards are those of the melody before it with the bass row in place of the violin's (the guard of B2 is 1000 N where it was 100 N). By the flyback reader the bow slips fast once per period at all three cells in G2, A2, C3 and D3, and twice per period in B2 (1.98 to 2.00, exactly one in 0.02 to 0.04 of its periods). Against the splice of real notes the site's analysis reads, bass row against the violin row it replaces: noise floor -2.3 dB against -13.4, harmonicity -4.65 dB against -5.56, wobble -0.6 cents against 5.5, and worse on attack (ratio 0.37 against 0.43), brightness (0.76 against 0.79), level (-6.6 dB against -5.5), timbre distance (9.3 dB against 8.9), onset roughness (0.04 against 0.01), partials (9.1 dB against 9.0) and envelope correlation (0.757 against 0.777)

a measured bass: the body is mapped from a maker's published specification onto the il Cannone specimen tables, not scanned; the bass bar is moved 18.1 mm inward to clear the f-hole (no source prints that position), and its width is 20 mm on the cards (Johannsson's 850 x 20 mm) where a luthier's 4/4 bass specification sheet (Goldblatt) and the bass observed in Pantelić's thesis print 25 mm, so the width is a spread of 20 to 25 mm that no render carries the upper end of; the outer-string bridge spacing is likewise a spread of 85 to 87 mm (Johannsson 85 mm, the A1 card 85.5 mm, Goldblatt's 4/4 column 87 mm), and no render carries 87; the bridge is a uniform 152.6 g shell; the 1.070 m of a 3/4 instrument is not modelled
measured wood properties below 150 Hz (maple) and 100 Hz (spruce)

string torsion: the cards carry no twist modes
the rosin's temperature and contact history: the friction is a steady sliding curve with no thermal or third-body memory

a printed double-bass after-length: the 0.184 of the G2, D3, Eb2, Db4 and A1 pages is one photograph's reading (+-7 %, 0.171 to 0.197; the body-scale reading of the same photograph, 0.178, and a luthier's table that prints 200 mm for a 3/4 bass are other readings that no render carries), and the 116/115 ratio that the earlier pages took is the cello's, borrowed, and the restored D2 page still takes it (the restored E1 page takes one sixth of the speaking length, a printed rule)
player variation: bow speed and force follow a fixed schedule

the bridge's support stiffness: a spring from the string's bridge node to the body is an opt-in row of the engine, and its stiffness K is not measured; two values a decade apart disagree. On the one-string A1 card, at 0.856 of the string and undamped, K = 2e5 N/m gives a window rms (1.5 to 2.45 s of a 3 s render) 6.8 dB above the page's and an amplitude that beats with a period of about 1.25 s, K = 2e4 N/m gives 4.6 dB above and steady, and the levels of H1 to H8 differ from the page's by up to 15 dB and 24 dB; on 1 s renders of the same card (window 0.75 to 1.0 s, no row: rms 2600 LSB) K = 2e4, 2e5, 2e6 and 2e7 N/m give a window rms 4587, 7967, 6889 and 6806 LSB (4.9, 9.7, 8.5 and 8.4 dB above the same card without the row), and K = 2e7 against K = 2e6 moves the levels of H1 to H8 by at most 0.40 dB (K = 2e6 against the card without the row by 9.40 dB) and the first harmonic by 1.3 cents, so above about 2e6 N/m the sound stops depending on K at the decade scale, but not to the 0.1 dB and 0.2 cents that the rigid test asks; no page carries the row, which adds 8 dB to the window rms and up to 9 dB to single harmonics, until its stiffness is taken from a print with its force scale and driving point
